title: Symmetry
summary: A transformation that leaves a specified object unchanged relative to a specified action.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

assumptions.text: A group G acts on a set X.
An object x belongs to X.

content.plain: Symmetry is never just “looks the same”: one must specify which transformations are allowed and what counts as unchanged.
content.exact: The symmetry group of x relative to the action of G on X is Stab_G(x) = { g in G : g·x = x }.
content.example: A square in the Euclidean plane has rotations and reflections that map the square to itself.
content.caveat: Symmetry depends on the chosen object representation and transformation group.

relations.note: Invariants are quantities preserved by specified transformations.
Chirality is defined relative to transformation classes.

verification.method: Revision migration checked for exact-reference closure and editorial mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.
